docs.title: About
docs.text:
This is a complete documentation for creating entities in RLD+ with the help of the Entity module/class made by Avery.

The module is still work in progress and there will be more features to come.

docs.title: Constructing
docs.text:
Creating an entity is as follows: 

local Entity = require(path_to_module.Entity)

local EntityModel = path_to_model
local EntityData = {
    Speed = 25;
    SpawnLocation = 0;
    Direction = "Forward";
}

local myEntity = Entity.new(EntityModel,EntityData)

This will construct an entity with an existing model that has a speed of 25 studs/second, spawns at the first room and goes forward to the last room.

Note

When creating an entity using the .new constructor. The entity will not do anything because the entity isn't active.

To make an entity to start it's behaviour, do:

myEntity:Start()
This will make the entity to start it's actions based on your EntityData. If you want your entity to do custom actions or write your own code for your entity. Look at the coding section below.

docs.title: Coding
docs.text:
Normally, you would just write your own code for your entity to do specific actions. But when using the Entity class it becomes limited. To combat this, you can use the events that are created alongside your entity.

To make an entity do a certain thing when it reaches a room, do:

myEntity.OnRoomReached:Connect(function(roomNum: number)
    print("I",myEntity.Name,"has reached room number:",roomNum)
end)

To find out more about events, check the API Reference for events.

docs.title: new
docs.text:
{static}

Constructs an entity with an EntityModel and a valid EntityData setting. 

Entity.new(entityModel: Model,entityData: EntityData)
Parameters

entityModel : Model The model that the entity will use. It must contain at least one BasePart. entityData : EntityData The EntityData setting the entity will use.

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
{read-only}

The specified type for the entity. 

Entity.Type : string
This property is automatically set from the EntityData.

Info

There are 4 valid entity types: "Generic", "Checker", "Chaser", "Summoner"

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
{read-only}

The model that the entity is using. 

Entity.Model : Model
This property is automatically set from the constructor.

docs.title: Root
docs.text:
{read-only}

The entity's root part. 

Entity.Root : BasePart
This property is automatically set from the entity's Model.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
{read-only}

The entity's EntityData. 

Entity.Settings : EntityData
This property is automatically set from the constructor.

docs.title: State
docs.text:
Determines the entity's current state. 

Entity.State : string
This property can be modified directly or using Entity:ChangeState().

Warning

Changing the entity's state may cause unwanted behavior.

docs.title: Direction
docs.text:
{read-only}

The direction the entity is currently moving. 

Entity.Direction : string

Info

There are 2 valid directions: "Forward" and "Backward"

docs.title: CurrentRoom
docs.text:
{read-only}

The current room the entity is in. 

Entity.CurrentRoom : number
This is a dynamic property. Meaning it will change overtime.

docs.title: GetPosition
docs.text:
Returns the entity's position in Vector3 

Entity:GetPosition() : Vector3
Returns

Vector3 The entity's position.

docs.title: GetTarget
docs.text:
Returns the entity's MoveTo target. The MoveTo target can be set using Entity:MoveTo() 

Entity:GetTarget() : Vector3?
Returns

Vector3? The entity's MoveTo target.

Note

This method can return nil if there is no specified MoveTo target.

docs.title: CanSeeTarget
docs.text:
Returns true if the entity can detect a player in their hitbox radius or not. 

Entity:CanSeeTarget(target: Model|Player) : boolean
Parameters

target : Model | Player The target player to check.

Returns

boolean Describes whether the entity can detect the target player or not.

docs.title: IsPlayerHiding
docs.text:
Returns true if the player is hiding in one of the valid hiding spots. 

Entity:IsPlayerHiding(player: Player) : boolean
Parameters

player : Player The target player to check.

Returns

boolean Describes whether the player is currently hiding or not.

Note

If the player is hiding in one of the blacklisted spots. The method will return false.

docs.title: ChangeState
docs.text:
Force set the entity's current state. 

Entity:ChangeState(state: string) : ()
Parameters

state : string The state to set to the current state of entity.

Danger

This method can cause some of the entity's behavior to cancel or trigger. DO NOT MESS WITH THIS UNLESS YOU KNOW WHAT YOU'RE DOING.

docs.title: MoveTo
docs.text:
Make the entity move to a location. 

Entity:MoveTo(location: Vector3) : ()
Parameters

location : Vector3 The location to make the entity move to.

docs.title: MoveToRoom
docs.text:
{yields}

Make the entity move to a room number. 

Entity:MoveToRoom(roomNum: number) : ()
Parameters

roomNum : number The room number to make the entity move to.

docs.title: Destroy
docs.text:
Destroys the entity and disconnects all connections. 

Entity:Destroy() : ()

docs.title: SetPos
docs.text:
Set the entity's model to a position and an optional position for the entity to look at. 

Entity:SetPos(pos: Vector3, lookAt: Vector3?) : ()
Parameters

pos : Vector3 The world-space position to pivot the entity's model. lookAt : Vector3 The world-space point the entity should face toward.

Equivalent to CFrame.new(pos: Vector3,lookAt: Vector3)

docs.title: SetSetting
docs.text:
{recommended}

Set a setting from the EntityData the entity is using to a different value. This is useful If you want to change a certain entity's setting during runtime. 

Entity:SetSetting(setting: string,value: any) : ()
Parameters

setting : string The setting name to change. value : Variant The value to change to.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
{recommended}

Start the entity. 

Entity:Start() : ()

Note

If the entity's EntityData has no onInit function. This method is automatically called.

docs.title: OnStart
docs.text:
{deprecated}

Fires when the entity has started via :Start() 

Entity.OnStart (): Signal

Quote

I don't know why I added this. Since you can already code your own entity behaviour without needing this event. Avery 28/9/2026

docs.title: OnEnded
docs.text:
Fires when the entity has completed it's event sequence. 

Entity.OnEnded (): Signal

docs.title: OnHit
docs.text:
Fires when the entity successfully damages a player. 

Entity.OnHit (player: Player): Signal
Parameters

player : Player The player that was damaged.

docs.title: OnKill
docs.text:
Fires when the entity successfully kills a player. 

Entity.OnKill (player: Player): Signal
Parameters

player : Player The player that was killed.

docs.title: OnRoomReached
docs.text:
Fires when the entity enters a room. 

Entity.OnRoomReached (roomNum: number): Signal
Parameters

roomNum : number The room number that the entity entered.

docs.title: OnUpdate
docs.text:
Equivalent to RunSerivce.PostSimulation but fires after all entity core actions are called. 

Entity.OnUpdate (deltaTime: number): Signal
Parameters

deltaTime : number The time (in seconds) that the current frame has stepped the physics simulation, not accounting for physics throttling.

docs.title: OnRebound
docs.text:
Fires whenever the entity rebounds (reached the last or starting room). 

Entity.OnRebound (rebounds: number): Signal
Parameters

rebounds : number The amount of times the entity rebounded.

docs.title: MoveToFinished
docs.text:
Fires whenever the entity has finished it's MoveTo action. 

Entity.MoveToFinished (reached: boolean): Signal
Parameters

reached : boolean Describes whether or not the entity has reached the move to location or got interrupted.

docs.title: StateChanged
docs.text:
Fires whenever the entity's state changes. 

Entity.StateChanged (state: string): Signal
Parameters

state : string The current state of the entity.

docs.title: EntityAdded
docs.text:
{static}

Fires when an entity is added via the constructor. 

Entity.EntityAdded (entity: Entity) : Signal
Parameters

entity : Entity The entity that was added.

docs.title: EntityRemoved
docs.text:
{static}

Fires when an entity is removed via the :Destroy() method. 

Entity.EntityAdded (entity: Entity) : Signal
Parameters

entity : Entity The entity that was removed.

docs.title: Spawning
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    SpawnLocation = 0;
    SpawnOffset = Vector3.new(0,25,0);
}
This will make the entity spawn at the starting room (a.k.a Room 0) and offsets it's spawn location 25 studs on the Y axis.

Tip

To make the entity spawn at the last room, set the SpawnLocation to game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedVariables._NUMBER.Value.Value

Warning

We currently don't have a better implementation for spawning entities at the current room. This may be subject to change in the future or not.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Speed = 50;
    Direction = "Forward";
    Rebounds = 1;
}
This will make the entity move forward (from the starting room to the last room) at 50 studs per second and rebounds once.

docs.title: Blacklisting hiding spots
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    ProhibitedSpots = {}
}
The ProhibitedSpots setting will make it so that any players that are hiding in a spot that has been added to the ProhibitedSpots array are considered not hiding and the entity will attempt to damage/chase the player depending on the entity's type.

To add a hiding spot to be excluded from valid hiding spots, do: 

EntityData = {
    ProhibitedSpots = {"Table","your_hiding_spot_id"} -- Add more excluded hiding spots here
}

Info

List of hiding spots ids: "Table","Locker","BlueLocker"

docs.title: Damaging
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    DamagePerRate = 20;
    DamageDelay = 0.5; -- in seconds
    HitboxRadius = 14;
    Raycasting = true;
}
This will make the entity damage players by taking 20 points of their health every 0.5 seconds and has a radius of 14 studs.

The Raycasting setting will make it so that entities can only damage players if the entity is in line of sight of the player. However, if the player is hiding, the entity will not damage them unless they're hiding in one of the ProhibitedSpots

docs.title: Jumpscaring
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Jumpscare = "entity_name"
}
This will jumpscare the player with the specified Jumpscare setting. By default, the jumpscare will trigger when the player dies.

docs.title: Screen Shake
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Screenshake = {
        ['Range'] = 10,
        ['Strength'] = 0,
        ['Roughness'] = 15,
        ['FadeIn'] = 0.25,
        ['FadeOut'] = .65,
        ['V3_PosInfluence'] = Vector3.zero,
        ['V3_RotInfluence'] = Vector3.new(1,1,2)
    }
}

Entities use CameraShaker module for visualizing camera shake. Check out CameraShaker's devforum post to learn more about how to use it.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text: Entities are designed to be fully customizable. Aside from basic settings, you can code your own entity to do whatever you want it to do.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Entities have events that you can listen for and respond to. They fires in response to specific actions or changes.

For example, an entity has rebounded: 

Entity.OnRebound:Connect(function(rebounds: number, direction: string)
    print("The entity has rebounded",rebounds,"times and is heading",direction)
end)
Or, an entity has finished it's sequence and about to be unloaded: 
Entity.OnEnded:Connect(function()
    print("The entity has completed")
end)
Or, an entity damages a player: 
Entity.OnHit:Connect(function(player: Player)
    print("The entity dealt damage to",player)
end)

docs.title: Entity Types
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Type = "Generic" -- this is a required setting, put your entity type in here
}
Aside from general entities, there are other variety of entity types like Hiding Spot Checkers, Summoners and Chasers. Each type has their own properties but are mostly inherited by the Generic type.

Warning

The Type setting is required and must be included in every EntityData setting module.

Check the API Reference for more info on different Entity types.
